levels.low: No ownership or role checks. Any authenticated user can read any other user's full record (including sensitive fields) and call admin-only endpoints.
levels.medium: BOLA: GET checks ownership, but POST body user_id overrides the session. BFLA: admin role read from query string (?role=) instead of session.
levels.high: BOLA: individual record access fixed for GET/POST, but GET /api/users/ lists all users with sensitive fields. BFLA: X-Role header overrides session role.
levels.impossible: Ownership enforced from session only. User list returns only public fields. Role from session only. No header or query override.

hints.low: Try accessing another user's profile. Is there any check to see if the resource belongs to you?
hints.medium: The GET request is protected, but what about other HTTP methods? Are there request parameters that can influence which record is returned?
hints.high: Individual records are protected. Is there a list endpoint? What does it return? Also, check request headers — does the server trust any that shouldn't be trusted?
hints.impossible: Nothing to bypass. Notice how the impossible level handles role checking and what fields are exposed in the user list.

low.note: Authenticated as alice (user 1), GET /api/users/2 to read bob's record.

medium.note: POST /api/users/2 with user_id=2 in the body, while session is user 1.

high.note: GET /api/users/ exposes all users' salary. Also try X-Role header on admin endpoint.
